Derivative-Free Optimization 1: First Problems¶

Sometimes the function you want to minimise has no usable gradient: it comes from a simulation, it has kinks, it is noisy, or it is simply code you would rather not differentiate. Derivative-free methods ask only for function values. After this chapter you can minimise a function with solve_dfo, read the result, understand which method Auto picks and why, control the budget, and repeat a run exactly.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program. Evaluation and iteration counts are shown because they are the same on every machine; no running times are claimed.

The mental model¶

A derivative-free method only ever asks “what is f at this point?”. From the answers it builds a picture of where lower values lie, and moves there. That makes it:

  • Cheap to set up. No gradient, no Hessian, nothing to derive or record.

  • Costly in evaluations. Without slope information it needs many more calls of f than a gradient method on a smooth problem. If your function is smooth and you can differentiate it, the gradient-based solvers of the earlier chapters will use far fewer evaluations.

  • Robust to rough functions. Kinks, plateaus and noise do not break it.

The methods fall into three families:

Family

Solvers

Idea

Simplex

NelderMead

a small shape of n+1 points that reflects, expands and shrinks along the valley

Direct search

PatternSearch, OrthoMads, LtMads, MadsAdvanced

poll points around the best one on a mesh; refine the mesh when no poll improves

Population

DifferentialEvolution, DifferentialEvolutionPrmm, ParticleSwarm, ParticleSwarmDv

many points explored at once, recombined or pulled toward the best found

Bounds and constraints are optional everywhere. Leave lower_bounds, upper_bounds, constraints and constraints_values unset and the problem is unconstrained; every program in this chapter does exactly that.

The pieces¶

Piece

Meaning

DfoProblem::initial

starting point (a one-dimensional Series); also fixes the number of variables

DfoProblem::objective

Series -> Series returning one number

lower_bounds, upper_bounds

optional box

DfoOptions::solver

Auto (default) or a named method

max_evaluations, max_iterations

budgets; 0 means the method’s own default

relative_improvement_tolerance

stop when progress falls below this; 0 means the method’s own default

rng_seed

seed for every random draw (default 5489)

Result field

Meaning

minimizer, minimum

the best point found and its objective value

status

Converged, ReachedIterationBudget, ReachedEvaluationBudget, ReachedTimeBudget, InfeasibleStationary

selected_solver, selection_reason

the method that ran and, for Auto, why

diagnostics

evaluations, iterations, and method-specific counters

Checklist¶

  1. Start with solve_dfo and Auto; read selected_solver and selection_reason.

  2. Look at status. Anything but Converged means a budget ended the run.

  3. Count diagnostics.evaluations; this, not wall time, is the cost to plan around.

  4. Fix rng_seed when you need to reproduce a run.

  5. If the function is smooth and differentiable, ask whether a gradient-based solver would do the job in a fraction of the evaluations.
